name: Diagnostic_INT-VSR
questiontext:
The area between the curve {{CT:0}}, the \(y\)-axis and the lines \(x={{CT:1}}\) and \(x={{CT:2}}\) is revolved once around the \(x\)-axis. Find the volume of revolution of the solid swept out. [[input:ans1]]

[[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
Recall that the volume swept out by a curve \(y(x)\) revolved once around the \(x\) axis, and between the lines \(x=a\) and \(x=b\) is given by: \[\mbox{Volume} = \pi \int_a^b y(x)^2\,dx.\]

 So the volume swept out in this question is:

 \[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
 \pi\int_{{CT:1}}^{{CT:2}} \left({{CT:3}}\right)^2 \, dx&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle
 {{CT:4}} \int_{{CT:1}}^{{CT:2}} {{CT:5}} \, dx,\\
 &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle
 {{CT:4}} \int_{{CT:1}}^{{CT:2}} \left({{CT:6}}\right) \, dx,\\
 &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle
 \left[ {{CT:7}}\right]_{{CT:1}}^{{CT:2}},\\
 &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:8}}. \end{array}\]
prtpartiallycorrect: You may have made a common mistake.
